qa.title: Q988 (Nov. 15, 2024)
qa.question: If I have a Delta Cannon in my cemetery, and I summon Tetra, Sapphire Rebel, in what order should I resolve their abilities?
qa.answer: Since both abilities are triggered simultaneously, you may resolve them in any order. However, if there are 4 cards in your EX area, the order in which you decide to resolve them determines which card is put into your EX area. If you decide to resolve Tetra, Sapphire Rebel's Fanfare ability first, you will put a Repair Mode into your EX area. Then, since your EX area is full, you can't put Delta Cannon into your EX area with its automatic ability. Likewise, if you decide to resolve Delta Cannon's automatic ability first, you will put it into your EX area. Then, since your EX area is full, you can't put a Repair Mode into your EX area with Tetra, Sapphire Rebel's Fanfare ability.

qa.title: Q1037 (Nov. 15, 2024)
qa.question: I attack an enemy Underworld Watchman Khawy with this follower and both are destroyed. If I resummon this follower and evolve it with its Last Words ability, can my opponent destroy it with the Last Words ability of their Underworld Watchman Khawy?
qa.answer: Yes. Both this follower and the enemy Underworld Watchman Khawy are destroyed at the same time, triggering both Last Words abilities. Since you are the active player, you must resolve your pending abilities before your opponent can resolve theirs. Therefore, the evolved version of this follower will be on the field when your opponent resolves the Last Words ability of their Underworld Watchman Khawy.

qa.title: Q1036 (Nov. 15, 2024)
qa.question: I put this follower into my EX area from an opponent's cemetery with the On Evolve ability of Octrice, Omen of Usurpation. If I summon this follower, then it is destroyed, how should I resolve this follower's Last Words ability?
qa.answer:
If you pay the cost of this follower's Last Words ability, it will be put onto its owner's field before being banished.

1. When this follower is destroyed, it goes into its owner's cemetery.
2. When it is put into the cemetery, its Last Words triggers, and you can choose whether or not to pay its cost.
3. If you choose to pay the cost, you would banish a Naterran Great Tree from your field or EX area.
4. You would then put this follower onto your opponent's field engaged.
5. You would then evolve it. However, it can only be evolved by revealing its evolved form from its master's evolve deck. It is on your opponent's field, so your opponent is its master, and their evolve deck is a private zone, so you can't evolve it.
6. Since this follower wasn't evolved, it would be banished.

qa.title: Q1024 (Nov. 15, 2024)

qa.answer: Yes. Although you can only activate one evolve ability per turn, other abilities that evolve followers do not count towards this limit.
